## Economic Research Data Visualization

```{ojs}
//| echo: false
//| panel: input

// This is Observable JS code for a dynamic visualization
// This would execute when the site is rendered with Quarto

viewof yearFilter = Inputs.range(
  [2015, 2025],
  {value: 2025, step: 1, label: "Year:"}
)

viewof metricSelector = Inputs.radio(
  ["Participation Rate", "Average Donation", "Total Donations"],
  {value: "Participation Rate", label: "Metric:"}
)
```

// Create the chart based on selected metric
Plot.plot({
  height: 500,
  color: {
    legend: true
  },
  y: {
    grid: true,
    label: metricSelector === "Participation Rate" ? "Participation Rate (%)" :
           metricSelector === "Average Donation" ? "Average Donation (€)" :
           "Total Donations (€)"
  },
  marks: [
    Plot.line(data, {
      x: "year",
      y: metricSelector === "Participation Rate" ? d => d.participationRate * 100 :
         metricSelector === "Average Donation" ? "avgDonation" :
         "totalDonations",
      stroke: "country",
      strokeWidth: 3,
      curve: "natural"
    }),
    Plot.dot(data, {
      x: "year",
      y: metricSelector === "Participation Rate" ? d => d.participationRate * 100 :
         metricSelector === "Average Donation" ? "avgDonation" :
         "totalDonations",
      stroke: "country",
      fill: "country"
    })
  ]
})

### About This Visualization

This interactive visualization displays charitable giving data from my field experiments conducted in Morocco, Egypt, and the UK from 2015 to 2025. You can:

1. Adjust the year slider to see how donation patterns evolved over time
2. Switch between different metrics (participation rate, average donation amount, and total donations)
3. Compare trends across different countries

This visualization demonstrates how cultural contexts and interventions affect charitable giving behaviors across diverse populations. The data reveals interesting patterns in donation participation rates and giving amounts that align with my research on religious norms and charitable giving behaviors.

## Available Research Datasets

The following datasets from my published research are available for academic use. Please cite the original papers when using these data.

| Paper | Dataset | Description |
|-------|---------|-------------|
| @dertwinkel-kaltConcentrationBiasIntertemporal2021 | @dertwinkel-kaltReplicationPackageConcentration2021 | Laboratory experiment data on concentration bias in intertemporal choice, including decision tasks and demographic data |
| @lambarraaNormsCharitableGiving2015 | @rienerReplicationDataFatima2022 | Field experiment data from Morocco examining religious norms in charitable giving behavior |
| @reinsteinDecomposingDesertTangibility2011 | @rienerReplicationDataReinstein2022 | Experimental data decomposing desert and tangibility effects in charitable giving |

## Data Management and Sharing Policy

I am committed to open science practices and transparent research. All data from my published research is made available through appropriate repositories after a reasonable embargo period. Research data is archived according to the FAIR principles (Findable, Accessible, Interoperable, and Reusable).

For inquiries about accessing data from ongoing projects or unpublished research, please contact me at [g.riener@soton.ac.uk](mailto:g.riener@soton.ac.uk).
